hook_candidates.spoken: Why do you hear thunder only after the flash?
Thunder takes about five seconds to travel a mile.

sources.title: US National Weather Service, Understanding Lightning: Thunder: the lightning discharge heats the air rapidly and causes it to expand; the sound of thunder takes about 5 seconds to travel a mile; count the seconds between flash and thunder and divide by 5 for the distance in miles; you should be in a safe place while counting; if you can hear thunder, chances are that you're within striking distance of the storm
sources.label: US National Weather Service

sources.title: Met Office, Thunder and lightning: thunder is the sound produced by the rapid heating of air by a lightning strike; thunder is always heard after the lightning is seen because light travels significantly faster than sound; seconds between flash and thunder divided by five give the approximate distance in miles, divided by three in kilometres
sources.label: Met Office (UK)

sources.title: NOAA National Severe Storms Laboratory, Severe Weather 101: Lightning: count the seconds from the flash until you hear thunder; divide by 5 for the miles to the flash, by 3 for kilometers
sources.label: NOAA NSSL

layout.description: Plümo thought thunder just dawdles. Wrong: light travels much faster than sound. Seconds between flash and thunder divided by three give roughly the distance in kilometers. Count from a safe place: if you can hear thunder, you're probably within striking distance.

beats.spoken: Lightning and thunder don't arrive together. I count from inside. At the window.
Wait. I thought thunder just dawdles and starts late. But no late start. Light travels much faster than sound. I was shocked. I fetched my stopwatch. Indoors.
What is thunder? Lightning heats the air fast, and the air expands. Thunder is that sound. It takes about five seconds to travel a mile. No hands, so I point with my leaf.
Closer. Count the seconds between flash and thunder. Divide by five for roughly the miles, by three for the kilometers. It's a rule of thumb. I have no thumbs.
And the most important part: be in a safe place while counting. I count inside, at the window. If you can hear thunder, you're probably within striking distance. With a cushion.
Remember: seconds divided by three, roughly the kilometers. And you count indoors. Right, my turn. Stopwatch on. Result: courage unknown. I guess I got startled.
I'll just lie here for a bit. More Zonkfruit? Follow the channel. I'll get up in a minute.
